prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: Building on c018 (cap 3.92, TNS-heavy, score +0.505, best so far), the cap is already the only active lever in this patch; nudge it modestly downward by x0.7 to ~2.74 so weight concentrates further on the most-critical nets and spreads moderate-violation reduction, confirming whether the trend of tighter caps continues to help TNS without harming legality.
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.323 robust(mean-std)=+0.081 min_case=+0.075 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.075 dWNS=+17.4% dTNS=+1.2% overflow~118
  bp-ng45: score=+0.107 dWNS=+8.4% dTNS=+11.9% overflow~122
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.141 dWNS=+8.4% dTNS=+17.7% overflow~136
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: tightening the cap to ~2.74 improved TNS across all three cases (dTNS +1.2% to +17.7%) with all runs valid, confirming the tighter-cap trend. Gains are broadest on bp_fe-ng45 (score +0.141, dTNS +17.7%) and bp-ng45 (+11.9%), consistent with concentrating weight on critical nets while still reducing moderate violations; ariane133-ng45 shows only marginal TNS (+1.2%) despite strong dWNS (+17.4%), suggesting its TNS is dominated by many moderate nets the tighter cap under-serves. Next step: test an intermediate cap (~3.2) or a case-adaptive cap to recover ariane's TNS without losing the bp gains.
